questions.question:
**In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

questions.solution:

__
 
• The simple present tense is used when an action is happening right now, **to state or ask about things in general, **or when it happens regularly or unceasingly.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V1 + object.
 
 
 
• The verb will take 's/es' if the given noun/pronoun (3rd person) is singular.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He plays badminton daily.*
 
 
 
• In the given part of the sentence, we need a simple present verb tense as a general statement has been given here.
 
• Since 'freedom' is a singular noun, the singular verb i.e., 'means' will be used.

Correct Sentence__: *Freedom of expression **means **the right to express one’s own convictions and beliefs.*

• ​See, think, know, possess, like, want, desire, hate, seem, imagine, etc.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​My brother is owning a car. (incorrect)*
 
• *​My brother owns a car. (correct)*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Sitab asked his mother, “Has it been snowing all night?”

options.text: Sitab asked his mother if it had been snowing all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it has snowed all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it was snowing all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it is snowing all night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **Sitab asked his mother if it had been snowing all night.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​​

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:

 
 
• When the direct speech is in the interrogative form, we follow the steps given below:
 
• When the reporting verb 'said to' is used without an object, it is used as it is.
 
• Comma and inverted commas are replaced by the connective word 'if'.
 
• Change the sentence in the reported speech from interrogative to assertive.
 
• ​The helping verb is changed according to the tense, followed by the 3rd form of the verb. The present perfect continuous tense will be changed to the past perfect continuous tense.
 
 
• has been snowing - had been snowing.
 
 
 
 
 
• ​At last, line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get - *Sitab asked his mother if it had been snowing all night. *

• Sentence B tells us more about the** two decorated elephants​. **They escort the Emperor and head the possession.** **So, **Sentence B** will be put in second place.
 
• Sentence A tells about the **camels carrying drums and small guns **and they are behind the two elephants (**'them' **refers to the elephants).

• The last sentence is C as it mentions the **platoons of soldiers that are 'at the end.'**

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The Delhi Police has shot an educational video on Traffic Rules for school students

options.text: An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students is being shot by the Delhi Police
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students was being shot by the Delhi Police.
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students has been shot by the Delhi Police.
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students had been shot by the Delhi Police.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students has been shot by the Delhi Police.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the active voice, hence we need to convert it into the passive voice.
 
• Find the subject (The **Delhi Police**) and object (**An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students**) of the sentence and exchange their places. 
 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect **tense. The passive verb form for the present perfect is: 
 
 
• Has/have + been + past participle form of the verb.
 
• So, '**has shot**' changes to '**has been shot**'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get - *An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students has been shot by the Delhi Police. *
